messages:
maya: FYI ticket #TI-4829 from tenant-987 — they started seeing sustained 429s around 09:02 UTC, spikes every minute for ~20m. customer says traffic didn’t change on their side.

jenny-cs: I got the initial logs. They send ~120 RPM normally, spiking to ~5k RPM for a few seconds according to their proxy metrics. They’re on our shared hosted plan.

alex: Can you paste the first 429 response headers and the request id? need x-request-id + x-rate-limit headers to confirm which limiter fired.

jenny-cs: Paste from the customer: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 09:02:14 GMT
x-request-id: r-5f7a9b2c
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 60
x-rate-limit-tier: shared-hosted
```

alex: That looks like the global minute window cap hit (reset at 60). But curious they say traffic didn’t change — could be multiple clients aligning on minute boundary. Any sign of many concurrent HTTP/2 streams or multiplexing?

maya: Customer attached a short curl replay. They use an SDK that opens 8 concurrent streams and a bulk worker that fans out per item.

samir: Two quick theories: 1) client-side concurrency + tight retry loops produced a raft of requests at top-of-minute, or 2) upstream proxy (customer or CDN) batched heartbeats and released them in a micro-burst. Either way it looks like their requests exceeded the per-tenant token refill in a short window.

alex: Can we repro by replaying with similar concurrency? jenny, can you ask them for a short pcap or exact retry timings? otherwise we can simulate with 8 workers * 100 rps each for 10s.

jenny-cs: On it. I’ll ask for a timeline and whether they use default SDK retry. Also requested the SDK version.

deploy-bot: @channel New deployment: ratecap-dashboard v1.8 rolled at 08:40 UTC — includes extra per-tenant histograms. If we have logs for tenant-987 they might be richer now.

maya: Good — can we pull per-tenant refill traces for 09:00–09:10? want to confirm the token-bucket refill_ms and burst window.

alex: Pulled a quick trace: tenant-987 shows refill rate 2.0 tokens/sec with bucket_size 180. During the spike their incoming instantaneous rate hit ~450 tokens/sec for ~6s. Bucket drained -> 429 cascade. The interesting bit: our edge proxies upstream have a misaligned smoothing window: multiple proxies seem to reset their local windows at slightly different offsets which can cause stair-step 429s instead of evenly spread rejections.

samir: That explains the pattern in their graph — repeated short bursts every minute where proxies hand off a backlog. Workarounds: reduce client concurrency (concurrency=2), add randomized jitter to retries, and space out bulk jobs by adding a small randomized delay per item.

maya: Also suggest short-term: approve a temporary quota bump for tenant-987 (shared-hosted) to absorb the burst while they patch their client. If they need sustained capacity, recommend Dedicated.

alex: For platform fix: we should add cross-proxy smoothing to the refill logic or increase the per-tenant short-burst allowance to avoid pathological alignment. Filing infra ticket.

jenny-cs: Customer asked for specific retry guidance. Suggested parameters I sent: exponential backoff with jitter, max attempts 3, base 300ms, jitter=uniform(0,200ms), and set sdk concurrency to 2 for bulk upload flows.

maya: Perfect. I’ll send the steps to the customer and offer the temporary quota bump for 2 hours while they deploy SDK change. Keep me posted if we get more 429s after that.

samir: Note for the runbook: add a quick repro script we can hand to customers that simulates concurrent streams and shows the minute-boundary spike so they can verify fixes locally.

alex: Created INFRA-2147 to track cross-proxy smoothing + monitoring alert for >50% of tenant requests rejected as 429 in a 2m window.

jenny-cs: Customer replied: implementing SDK change now, will test in 15m. Thanks. :thumbsup:
